      "observations": [
        "The patch moves drawInTitlebar and autoHideTabbar controls and their unchanged Boolean preference IDs to Appearance, updates registration there and removes duplicate General registration. The unified-toolbar settings button now opens paneAppearance/layoutGroup, and the moved checkbox task targets the same location. It reorganizes scrolling, language/fonts, underline-links and plaintext controls within General without an exhaustive migration claim.",
        "Independent top-level Appearance fieldsets separate window layout from message-list controls and the notification-box group. Current preferences category switching iterates paneDeck direct children and compares data-category, supporting that local grouping boundary. Reviewer search-clutter rationale was qualified by uncertainty and shared notification needs; no full text-search implementation or search usability run is claimed.",
        "The changed tests move the glyph scroll target, rename the language/fonts category target, add layout checkbox toggles, and scroll receipts button then await a frame before opening it. Current helper directly checks checkbox state/preference values across both initial states and two toggles; this does not assert actual native titlebar/tabbar rendering or all moved settings.",
        "Review requests avoiding assertions in setup, decoupling groups and fixing indentation. The reviewer later commandeers the revision and says feedback addressed, then reports a Windows browser_general failure followed by good Try. Actual final Git retains mixed indentation in parts; that critique is not an accepted indentation rule. Screenshot metadata and design approval are not independently inspected pixels or accessibility proof.",
        "Current source keeps the pane/shortcut/control contracts, with later Fluent label changes and other additions. The initial title says all relevant options, but author description explicitly says only some moved and more remains. No defaults, preference migrations or product behavior equivalence are inferred from relocation alone."
      ],
